questions.prompt: Iris, Cal, and Theo are talking. Iris and Cal trade quick lines. Theo speaks once. What pattern is forming?

options.label: Alliance — two voices close on the third.
Balanced — everyone gets equal air time.

questions.mentorPostScript: An alliance shape isn't wrong. Lean in or break out — your call.

questions.prompt: When one of the three characters is being talked AROUND rather than TO, what is the dialogue doing?

options.label: Showing exclusion. The quiet is its own line of dialogue.
Wasting space — give every speaker equal lines.
Breaking the rules of branching dialogue.

questions.mentorPostScript: What does the quiet character notice while the other two talk?

questions.prompt: Theo is the arbiter — they step between Iris and Cal when the argument crosses a line. Which line sounds most arbiter-like?

options.label: "Hey — let's stop for a beat. What just happened here?"

questions.mentorPostScript: The arbiter names what just happened before suggesting what's next.

questions.prompt: Across three characters, what makes each voice recognizably distinct from the others?

options.label: Signature words + rhythm + register the others don't use.
Always ending sentences with an exclamation point.

questions.mentorPostScript: Each character should have a fingerprint — three lines you'd recognize even without a tag.

options.label: You have to keep three voices distinct AND keep them in conversation with each other.
Three is just too many for any story.

questions.mentorPostScript: Three voices, three shapes — alliance, jealousy, arbitration. Each is its own draft of the same scene.
